alignments.note: Postpositive γάρ realized by the verse-opening For.
Inflected verb takes its English subject pronoun as a rule 7/9 helper; head on the lexical verb know.
Reported speech with an expressed complementizer, so rule 43's unrepresented case does not apply.
Intensifying καί written out as even (rule 65's English-side test); no correlative οὕτως or comparative stands, so rules 82 and 100 are not in question.
Adverb on its own English word; the ASV places it after the supplied subject.

Circumstantial participle rendered as a finite clause: the supplied subordinator when and subject he are rule 7 helpers on the participle under rule 86, which places a supplied when on a participle. Head on the lexical verb desired; discontinuous around t008 under rule 15.
Infinitival to is rule 7's helper on its own verb, no conjunction governing the clause (rules 40, 61).
Article surfaces as the (rule 19); split from its noun under rule 26.
Noun stands alone, its determiner having gone to the article.
Aorist passive with its English subject and auxiliary; rule 9 heads on the lexical participle rejected.
Second γάρ realized by for introducing the explanatory clause.
Verb with its supplied subject pronoun; head on found.

The ASV writes the clause negation once, as no on the object. τόπον is a plain noun and not a negative indefinite, so rules 41 and 59 do not empty the negator; the single English negative answers to οὐχ and place answers to the noun, so the two stay separate under rule 2.
Noun on its own English word, the negation having gone to οὐχ.

One Greek noun rendered by an English phrase: the supplied case preposition for and the determiner a are rule 7/21 helpers on the noun, no article standing in the Greek. Rule 66 heads on the word that glosses the lexeme; change is what μετάνοια's shift-of-mind sense turns on, mind naming only the domain. Heading on mind remains defensible and is the competing reading.

The ASV's italicized in his father is an interpretive supply: no source token in this verse or a neighbouring one licenses it (rule 5), αὐτήν being already spent on it at t033. Rule 37 is not the case, since the phrase answers to no Greek anywhere in the projection.
Concessive conjunction realized by though (rule 40).

Participle with its supplied subject; the ἐκ- intensive is realized by diligently, which belongs to this token and not to any other. Discontinuous around t033 under rule 15; head on the verb word sought, which is what the corpus spends on ζητ- (rule 91).
Object pronoun on its own English word.
Preposition realized by with (rule 36); the ASV spreads the phrase over two words, so rule 94 keeps the pair split.
Governed noun on its own English word.

review_notes: All 20 source ids and all 36 target ids are partitioned exactly once.
The one added unit is the ASV's italicized in his father; every other supplied English word (when, he, to, a, for, diligently) is attached to the source token that licenses it under rule 7.
οὐχ is aligned to no rather than left unrepresented: rules 41/59 empty a negator only before a second negative word, and τόπος is not one.
The head of the μετανοίας unit is contestable between change and mind; the note names the competing reading.
The verse note's alternative punctuation (place of repentance as one parenthesis) does not change the token-level alignment adopted here.
